where: Section 1, Section 2, Exam traps, Quiz Q6
problem: The powerset is written as 2Q and the bound as 2n. Read literally, 2Q is a set name and 2n means 2 times n, which is false for n ≥ 3 (an NFA with 5 states can give 32 DFA states, not 10). A student will copy the wrong bound.
fix: Use superscripts: δ: Q × (Σ ∪ {ε}) → 2<sup>Q</sup>, "the set of all subsets of Q"; "at most 2<sup>n</sup> states for an NFA with n states"; same fix in the exam trap "up to 2<sup>n</sup> states" and in the Quiz Q6 answer "At most 2<sup>n</sup> DFA states".

problem: Step 7 separates A from B and E from B, but never separates A from E. In the first round A and E look identical: on a, b, c both go to non-final states. So the jump to the groups {A}, {B}, {C,D}, {E} does not follow from what is shown, and a student may conclude A and E are equivalent and merge them, giving a wrong minimal DFA.
fix: Add the second round: after the first split the groups are {A,E}, {B}, {C,D}. Now on a, A goes to B (group {B}) while E goes to E (group {A,E}), so A and E split. Final groups: {A}, {B}, {C,D}, {E}.

problem: "The DFA before minimisation has 4 states A, B, C, D" contradicts step 6, where the dead state E was added to make the DFA complete before minimising; the automaton that was actually minimised has 5 states.
fix: Say: the partial DFA has 4 states A, B, C, D; with the dead state E the complete DFA has 5 states; the minimal partial DFA has 3 states A, B, F.

problem: "If for some symbol a their transitions land in different groups, split them into separate groups" suggests splitting every differing pair apart. Two states with identical behaviour can then be pushed into separate groups, and refinement never re-merges them, so the result would not be minimal.
fix: State the rule as regrouping: inside one group, put states with the same tuple of target groups (one entry per symbol) into the same new group, and states with different tuples into different new groups. Repeat until the groups stop changing.
